headline: $45,000 transfer from contingency to professional legal fees moves forward on a 6-1-1 vote.
summary: The transfer pays legal fees for the current FOIA complaint, after $20,000 was already moved from contingency. Bills so far are about $35,000, and more are expected. The cafeteria report showed lunch participation up at all three school levels. The Energize energy project still needs town council approval.
decisions: Moved items 4.1.1 through 4.1.4 of the financial reports to the full board, with no opposition.
Moved the $45,000 transfer from contingency to professional legal fees to the full board, 6-1-1.
Moved items 4.2.1 through 4.2.5 of the cafeteria reports to the full board, with no opposition.
discussion: Legal fees for FOIA complaint: Members asked whether costs would keep rising, and more bills are expected because the matter is not finished. Members also asked about a third-party option tied to the complaint, but it could not be discussed while the matter is open.

Cafeteria participation: Lunch participation rose at all three levels, to 48.63% at elementary, 55% at middle school, and 42.86% at high school. October showed a $43,000 loss, which was attributed to higher-than-expected labor costs.

Energize energy project: Meetings with the mayor, comptroller, and Electric Division are planned before the project goes to town council. Town council must approve it because the project includes bonding.

Budget reports: Presenters walked through contingency, benefits, tuition, transportation, and salary lines. The 2% fund balance will not move until the last fiscal year closes, probably December, maybe January.

Facilities projects: The facilities update reported the Dag elevator modernization is complete and the middle school boilers are running, with more work expected by spring. The Sheehan High School elevator replacement is on hold while design issues are worked through.
